Waggoners Campsite | Surrey Hills, near Farnham & Guildford
Welcome to Waggoners! Eco-Friendly Camping in the Surrey Hills, near Farnham & Guildford. Click 'Book Now' to secure your stay!
We are now closed until Easter 2027.
Our season dates and bookings will be available in early 2027.
Our lovely neighbour, The Waggon Sauna, remains open throughout the year   click here to book.
Waggoners is an off-grid, environmentally-conscious campsite nestled in the stunning Surrey Hills, between Farnham and Guildford. A peaceful, grassy field surrounded by wild woodlands, offering a tranquil escape close to nature. We are open Thursday, Friday, Saturday & Sunday nights plus bank holiday Mondays. Tents, roof tents & small off-grid campervans are welcome.
We like nature. We like birdsong. We like green spaces. Our campers do too. We deliberately keep our numbers low to ensure our guests have plenty of personal space and peace even when we re full. We want our campers to have a fun, happy time but if for you that means a noisy group, boozy games, loud music or late night chats, we re probably not the best fit for you. To understand the vibe of our campsite and the behaviour we expect please read the Waggoners Code .
The site is part of Hampton Estate, a rural, family-run estate dedicated to stewardship and environmental protection. Alongside rearing 100% pasture-fed beef, growing hops for beer, and planting numerous trees, we’ve designed our campsite to reflect our deep commitment to sustainability.
Many of the structures at Waggoners were crafted by our forestry team using wood from our own estate. The waste from our compost loos is recycled as fertiliser. Thanks to our extensive tree planting, we absorb more carbon than we emit as a business. We strive to recycle and reuse wherever possible so that Waggoners remains a conscious campsite with zero environmental footprint, providing a calm, nature-focused experience for all who visit.
Waggoners Campsite Group Policy: Waggoners is a peaceful, nature-focused campsite designed to offer a calm and relaxing experience for all our guests. To maintain this atmosphere, we kindly discourage large groups and parties. We do not allow any groups of more than 18 people, nor hen or stag parties. If you are planning to visit as a group, please keep your numbers small and be aware that you will be expected to be especially courteous to other campers. This means keeping noise to a minimum, respecting quiet hours, and ensuring your group does not impact the peaceful enjoyment of the site or the surrounding natural environment. Large gatherings or rowdy behaviour are not suitable for Waggoners and may result in your group being asked to leave. Thank you for helping us preserve the calm, welcoming spirit of Waggoners for everyone to enjoy.
Prices
£18 per person per night (13 years and over)
£10 per child per night (2 12 years)
Children under 2 are free
£7 per dog per night
Walking or riding to us? Email for your special backpacker-bikepacker rate.
For more information, email waggoners@hamptonestate.co.uk

pages.text:
FAQs | Waggoners Campsite
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need to book? Yes. Stays are pre-payment only and we are often full! We d hate to turn you away. Click on the Book Now button.
Is there a minimum stay? No. You can book for just one night if that s all you can fit in.
Why can t I book for longer? We are only open for long weekends: Thursday-Sunday nights, plus Monday nights on a bank holiday.
What time can I arrive? Between 1pm & 7pm. Please do not arrive any earlier it gives departing campers time to leave and us a chance to keep the site nice and clean and get ready for your arrival. If you cannot arrive before 7pm, please email before booking.
What time do I need to leave?  By 11am. When we are full or on closing day, we do have to be very strict about this.
Where do I pitch? We do not have designated pitches, nor allocate or reserve spaces. One big field with plenty of room for everyone you choose your spot! Please just keep tracks and footpaths clear and respect others personal space (6m is a good minimum space as a guide).
Can I arrive by bicycle? Absolutely! We are close to some great cycling routes and have our lovely cycle hut to store your bike. We even offer a reduced rate for bikepackers (and backpackers!) email before booking. And there is plenty of room for kids to ride their bikes too, watching out for vehicles of course and being mindful that little wheels can pick up some speed down the slope!
Do you accept roof tents?  Yes!
Are campervans allowed? Yes, but we only accept smallish (no longer than 6m, no higher than 2.8m) off-grid campervans. Please note we do not have any van facilities (waste, water or hook up). It s fine to bring an awning too.
What about motorhomes? Sorry but motorhomes, caravans and trailer tents are not allowed.
Can I sleep in my hammock? Yes! If you re travelling light, there s a corner of our woods which is perfect for a hammock/ tarp set up.
Where can I leave my car? You can park where you pitch but please only bring two vehicles per booking. We try to protect our peace, grass and planet by asking campers to minimise driving around the campsite, keeping to the vehicle tracks and driving slowly, with extreme caution.
Do you accept dogs? We welcome well behaved dogs. They must be kept on a lead at all times. Please clean up after your dog and put all dog poo, bagged, into the general waste bin. If your dog is disruptive or causes annoyance to other campers, we may have to ask you to leave. We have no limit to the number of dogs on the site, and we have footpaths popular with dog walkers along our boundaries, so if your dog is reactive to other dogs, people including children, it s likely that you, your dog and your fellow campers probably wouldn t have the best camping experience.
Are you family friendly? Very much so! We love to see kids enjoying our site but please keep a close eye on them, especially if they venture into the woods at the bottom of the field as a road backs onto those woods. Our big Sand Castle is definitely in bounds! Our site is very natural, and well nature isn t all that smooth and even, so there are some stingers and brambles around the edges and the ground is lumpy and bumpy in parts.
Can I have a firepit or BBQ? We do allow them (under watchful eyes!) but if the fire risk is deemed too great due to extended periods of hot weather, we reserve the right to ban them. Firepits can be rented from us these can be used to cook food or just for a fire pre-book as we only have a limited number. You may bring your own firepit or BBQ but it must be sufficiently off the ground so as not to damage the grass.  Disposable BBQs are not permitted. Logs can be purchased from us on-site, please don t take from our woodland habitats.
Is there drinking water? All water on the site is mains fed and safe to drink. No need to bring shop-bought water just refillable water containers. None of our water is heated.
Is there any electricity? We have no power on the campsite. Zero secret sockets that you can use to charge your phone, so charge up everything before you come (or even better, enjoy some device free time). A power bank might be useful to bring. Maybe a torch too. Please do not run your vehicle engine for charging whilst on site. Generators are not permitted.
Is there phone signal? Vodafone & O2 work well, EE not so much.
Do you have a shop?  There is no campsite shop (we only sell logs). The nearest convenience store is in Tongham.
Is there a fridge? Nope. We recommend you bring your own cool box.
What do I do with my rubbish?  Please reduce and separate all your rubbish into the appropriate bins: there are food, recycling and general waste bins located beside the wagon. We have no capacity for broken equipment please take it home with you. Please leave as little trace as possible, for others campers and the wildlife.
Is there a noise policy? Quiet time is from 10pm until 8am. Treat your fellow campers to a peaceful night canvas affords little noise protection!
Can I play music?  Outside of quiet hours, at a low level only (most of our campers would rather be able to hear the birds singing).
Are ball games allowed?  If there s space and it s not annoying (or hitting!) other campers, it s fine with us.
Can we explore everywhere? Please don t enter the field behind the North Downs Way or the woods behind the facilities (ensure your kids stay out too as this is a working part of the estate). The woods along the bottom of the field are ours and are free to roam. Off the site, please stick to footpaths. Nearby Puttenham Common is a large open access area of the estate, excellent for exploring.
Can I smoke or vape? Smoking or vaping isn t allowed in any public areas on the campsite. Please pick up and bin your cigarette butts. No smoking in the woodlands.
Can I fly my drone? Sorry, drones are not permitted.

Getting Here | Waggoners Campsite
How To Find Us
Address: Waggoners Campsite, Puttenham Road, Seale GU10 1HP
What3Words: ///gliding.recording.madder
By Bike or Car: From Puttenham, head west for 1.5 miles towards Seale. Once past Totford Lane look out for our entrance on the left hand side.
From Seale, head east towards Puttenham, after 0.5 miles you will see the signs for Waggoners on your right.
We are just just off National Cycle Network route 22. Email us for your bikepacker rate!
On Foot: We are literally on the North Downs Way, perfect for those wanting to arrive on foot. The National Trail runs along the edge of our site, about 5 miles from the start in Farnham, just west of Puttenham Common. Email us for your backpacker rate!
By Train: The nearest train stations are Guildford, Farnham, Wanborough, Ash and Godalming. Taxis will drop off at the Welcome Hut.
